cards.explanation: The answer is that he looks this way and that. The text says Moses looked "…this way and that…" and saw no one (Exodus 2:12). He checks around before he does anything else. I think this is a heavy moment, friends, and the text doesn't hurry past it.

The answer is sand. Moses looked this way and that, saw no one, struck down the Egyptian and hid the body in the sand (Exodus 2:12). This is a heavy moment, so I'll just say it plainly. And watch what happens next, bakers: the very next day a Hebrew asks him, "Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" (Exodus 2:14).

The answer is the one in the wrong. Moses asks that man, "Why are you attacking your companion?" (Exodus 2:13). He doesn't put the question to the other man. The text says it was the next day when Moses went out and saw two Hebrews fighting, and this time he speaks up.

The answer is the Egyptian Moses killed. The man says, "Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" (Exodus 2:14). He doesn't just push back on Moses. He brings up the Egyptian right alongside asking who made Moses ruler and judge. I think that question lands like a dropped tray of cookies, and everybody in the kitchen hears it.
The answer is True. The text says, "Then Moses was afraid…" (Exodus 2:14). The man's words hit him hard, friends. Moses thought the thing he had done had surely become known.
The answer is False. The text says Pharaoh "…sought to kill Moses." (Exodus 2:15). Word got to the top of Egypt, and the king did not shrug it off. That's why Moses ran, bakers.

The answer is Midian! Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian (Exodus 2:15). That's where he sat down beside a well. Keep that well in mind, friends, because the next scene gathers around it.

The answer is False! The text says Moses "…rose up to help them…" when the shepherds came along and drove the daughters away (Exodus 2:17). He doesn't stay out of it. He had been sitting beside that well (Exodus 2:15), and now he gets up to step in.

The answer is watered. Shepherds drove the daughters away, and Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock (Exodus 2:17). Look at the switch, friends. First he's sitting beside a well in a brand new land (Exodus 2:15). Then somebody needs help, and he's up and pulling water. I know that feeling. I once sat in a drawer for years, and the second somebody needed me, I was ready to work.

The answer is that he asks why they're home so early today. Reuel, the priest of Midian, asks, "Why have you returned so early today?" (Exodus 2:18). He noticed the timing first. Seven daughters walking in ahead of schedule will get any dad's attention, bakers.

The answer is False. The daughters tell their father, "An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds…" (Exodus 2:19). They say Egyptian, friends, and that's how they describe him. They also say he drew water for them and watered the flock.

The answer is to invite him to have something to eat. Reuel says, "Invite him to have something to eat." (Exodus 2:20). He asks his daughters to bring the man in for a meal. A good host knows what to do when someone has helped his family.
The answer is Zipporah. Reuel gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage (Exodus 2:21). A meal invitation turned into a wedding, friends. That's quite a result from showing up at a well.

The answer is that he's become a foreigner in a foreign land. Moses names his son Gershom, saying, "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land." (Exodus 2:22). He has a wife and a son now, and he still says that about himself. I think those words have some ache in them, bakers.

The answer is that it rises up to God. The text says "…their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God." (Exodus 2:23). Their groaning goes up to God Himself, friends. The Israelites cried out under their burden of slavery, and the cry went to Him.

The answer is True. The text says, "God saw the Israelites and took notice." (Exodus 2:25). Right before that, God heard their groaning and remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (Exodus 2:24). The people were noticed, bakers.
